questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers right away. Exit the road carefully and park as far off the road as possible so other drivers can see you. Open your hood to signal that your vehicle is disabled.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down, move out of the way, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move out of the way, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, slow down immediately. Create a clear path for the emergency vehicle and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.
Change lanes quickly.
Speed up.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, turning is especially dangerous. Approach turns and curves much slower than you normally would to stay in control.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a phone.
Adjusting the radio or CD player.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers need to focus completely on driving. Any other activity, no matter how small, takes your attention away from the road and creates danger.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: How fast your car is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on three things: your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the pavement.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on a downhill slope than smaller vehicles.
Need a tighter turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on an uphill slope than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks are large and heavy. They require much longer distances to stop than cars do.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Your headlights may be misaligned if one side of your car is higher.
A tire can be damaged if you drift onto the shoulder.
You may hydroplane if the shoulder is wet.
You could lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops onto the low shoulder, do not brake hard or turn sharply. This will cause you to lose control. Instead, ease back onto the road gently.

questions.question: You must keep proof of your liability insurance:

options.text: At your workplace.
In a bank safety deposit box.
In your vehicle whenever you are driving.
At your neighbor's house.

questions.correctAnswerText: In your vehicle whenever you are driving.
questions.explanation: State law requires all drivers to have liability insurance. You must carry proof of insurance in your car at all times. If a police officer asks for it and you cannot show it, you will get a ticket.

questions.question: If you drive while intoxicated and injure or kill another person, you:

options.text: Will only pay a fine.
Will only go to jail.
Will only lose your license.
May lose your license and go to jail.

questions.correctAnswerText: May lose your license and go to jail.
questions.explanation: Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous. If you cause an accident while drunk that injures or kills someone, you may go to jail for two to seven years, pay a $5,000 fine, and lose your license for five years.

questions.question: When an aggressive driver threatens you, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them in return.
Make a gesture to show your disapproval.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is behaving dangerously, stay calm. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures. Put as much distance between you and the aggressive driver as possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A left curve is ahead.
A series of curves is ahead.
An S-curve is ahead.
The road will be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will be slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect your driving?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It makes you feel overly confident.
It makes it hard to think clearly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows reaction time and impairs judgment. It also affects coordination, balance, and vision. Never drink and drive.

questions.question: What does a "No right on red" sign mean?

options.text: You may turn right even if the light is red.
You cannot turn right when the light is red.
This intersection has many traffic crashes.
You do not need to stop at a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn right when the light is red.
questions.explanation: A "No right on red" sign means you must not turn right at a red light. You must wait for a green light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.
Truck route to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?

options.text: They make turning harder.
They increase the risk of hydroplaning.
They increase your stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires make turning difficult, increase stopping distance, and increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: What should you do when a school bus stops with its stop arm extended?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Continue driving once you think kids are done exiting.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop arm out. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are usually not important.
They are only in construction zones.
They give drivers information.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give drivers information.
questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers stay in the correct lane, show safe passing areas, and warn about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What happens to drivers who drink alcohol before driving?

options.text: They are always aware of their risks.
They lose control of their body, mind, and vehicle.
They become better drivers.
They have faster reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: They lose control of their body, mind, and vehicle.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on highways?

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay alert and keep scanning the road. Do not focus on one spot for too long to avoid highway hypnosis.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver is behind you?

options.text: Get out of their way.
Make eye contact with the driver.
Speed up as they pass you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: Let an aggressive driver pass. Do not make eye contact or speed up. Getting out of their way is the safest choice.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your physical condition does not make you drive unsafely?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only within what your body can handle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your physical condition matters for safe driving. You should know your limits and only drive when it is safe.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When a school bus has flashing red lights.
When you are near an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass if you cannot see ahead clearly, if there is a curve or hill in the way, at an intersection, at railroad crossings, on bridges, or in no passing zones. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of the road with a median or turn lane between you.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Any distraction that takes your attention away from driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel can cause a crash.

questions.question: What is the correct way to change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, turn on your signal and check your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no other vehicle is in the lane you want to enter. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Give your body time to remove the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time to remove the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to lower your BAC is to wait and let your body get rid of the alcohol. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change your BAC.
